modal.title: Privacy and AI Veterinary Disclaimer
modal.picsBody: We handle your data in line with the data protection laws that apply where you are (for example, Hong Kong’s Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance or the EU GDPR). Your name, phone and email are used only by this platform and appointed animal welfare organisations to contact you, confirm the animal’s location and follow up on the rescue. They are never made public, sold or used for marketing. The animal photo, location and description are shown publicly so that rescuers and volunteers can help; please avoid capturing people’s faces, licence plates or house numbers. The photo and description are sent to Google Gemini for AI analysis. To access or delete your data, please contact the platform administrator.
modal.aiBody: PawPulse uses Google Gemini multimodal AI to help citizens and rescue teams with initial triage (P0/P1/P2) and equipment suggestions. It is not a formal diagnosis by a registered veterinarian.
modal.p0Intro: If the animal is bleeding heavily, unconscious after being hit by a vehicle, has a severe fracture or is struggling to breathe, do not wait for a reply from the app.

guide.title: On-site first aid guide
guide.subtitle: What to do first when you find a stray or injured animal
guide.safetyBody: Injured, frightened or pained animals may bite or scratch by instinct, even if they are normally gentle. Never pry open their mouth or pick them up by force!

watch.title: Stay nearby:
watch.body: Watch from a safe distance (2–3 m) so the animal doesn't panic and run into traffic or a drain.

warm.title: Keep it warm:
warm.body: In cold weather or if the animal has lost blood, cover it with a clean blanket or jacket.

report.title: Photograph & report:
report.body: Report with PawPulse so AI can assess injuries and match nearby NGOs.

water.title: A little water:
water.body: Only if the animal is alert and can lower its head by itself, offer a small amount of room-temperature water. Never force it.

move.title: Don't move it unnecessarily:
move.body: After a suspected road accident, moving the spine or pelvis can cause nerve damage or fatal internal bleeding.

feed.title: Don't give human food or milk:
feed.body: Many cats and dogs are lactose intolerant, and food in the stomach can cause choking if emergency anaesthesia is needed.

meds.title: Don't give medication:
meds.body: Human painkillers (e.g. paracetamol) are toxic to cats and dogs and especially deadly to cats. Don't apply creams either — the animal may lick them off.

crowd.title: Don't crowd around:
crowd.body: Crowds increase stress and may trigger shock or a desperate escape.
